'''Sim Aloo''' was a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] noted for his patience, wisdom, and silence. He served as an [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]] in the [[Office of the Supreme Chancellor/Legends|office]] of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] in the final [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Following Palpatine's [[Declaration of a New Order|reorganization]] of the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Aloo continued to serve the new [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] as his senior [[Politics/Legends|political]] [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|advisor]] in the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Emperor's Inner Circle]] for the duration of the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial era]]. Being [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-sensitive, he trained as a [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adept]].

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Aloo was one of six advisors who accompanied Palpatine on his journey to the incomplete [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]]. Within the [[Emperor's throne room|throne room]], Aloo and fellow Inner Circle member [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]] met with the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], a conference briefly interrupted by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Tiaan Jerjerrod/Legends|Tiaan Jerjerrod]], commander of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]. Plotting to destroy the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], Palpatine leaked the information of his own presence aboard the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] to the Alliance as bait, drawing them into a trap. The Alliance launched a full-scale [[Battle of Endor/Legends|attack]] on the construction site, but, contrary to Palpatine's expectations of an easy Imperial victory, the battle culminated with the destruction of the battlestation and Aloo's [[Death/Legends|death]].

==Biography==
===Republic bureaucrat===
Sim Aloo was a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]]<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Sim Aloo}}</ref> [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Homeworld/Legends|from]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="DB" /> Before the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], he came to be an ally of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who was secretly the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] Darth Sidious.<ref name="Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> Aloo continued to serve as an [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]] to Palpatine upon the latter's ascension to the position of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]], becoming one of the many beings comprising the [[Office of the Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Office of the Supreme Chancellor]]. In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Aloo was present among other consultants, including fellow advisors [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]] and [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]], in a meeting with the Chancellor. Together, they held up a group of delegates from the [[Loyalist Committee/Legends|Loyalist Committee]]&mdash;led by [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] of [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]], and [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of Naboo&mdash;who had previously scheduled an appointment with Palpatine. Organa noted that the Chancellor's tendency to isolate himself among his advisors was peculiar.<ref name="LOE" />

===Imperial advisor===
[[File:Sim_aloo.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Sim Aloo was known as a silent, yet wise, advisor to the Emperor.]]
Days later, as the Clone Wars reached its climax, Palpatine [[Declaration of a New Order|reorganized]] the Republic into the first [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], with himself as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> The transition had little effect on Aloo, who remained as an [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|advisor]] in Palpatine's [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Inner Circle]],<ref name="DB" /> a group of [[minister]]s and [[Governor/Legends|governors]] who had secured Palpatine's favor. Aloo was one of a select group of consultants who were allowed to privately discuss matters with the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]].<ref name="Insider96 Q&A">{{InsiderCite|96|Ask Lobot|Q&A: Motti the Barbarian?}}</ref> Noted for his wisdom and patience, he became the Emperor's senior [[Politics/Legends|political]] advisor<ref name="CCG" /> and served on the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Security Council]].<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> At one point, Aloo and Greejatus were featured in an advertisement for [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]]' latest [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]].<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref>

Aloo and his fellow dignitaries held considerable power within the command structure of the Empire. They were loyal to the Emperor, but the collective group of advisors, hundreds in all, was internally divided. The Emperor promoted this competition and managed to control the members of his inner circle through a web of fear and uncertainty. To further divide the advisors, the Emperor deliberately only met with up to a dozen at a [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="GG5">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> Aloo, as the Emperor's senior political consultant,<ref name="CCG" /> was one of the select few advisors who continually met with Palpatine, making lesser individuals feel insecure.<ref name="GG5" /> Additionally, he was one of many Inner Circle members to receive training in the ways of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] as Palpatine's [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]]; the Emperor planned to replace the various [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] and governors with the Adepts as he consolidated his control over [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="DSS" />

[[File:GreejatusAndFriends-ROTJ.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Aloo and Greejatus meet with the Emperor and Vader aboard the second Death Star.]]
In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="Kren's Galactic Files">{{Topps|set=2013 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files Series 2|cardname=Kren Blista-Vanee|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/93283/cid/6569552/2013-Topps-Star-Wars-Galactic-Files-Series-2-526-Kren-Blista-Vanee}}</ref> as the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] neared completion above the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]], Palpatine journeyed to the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] as part of an elaborate ploy to destroy the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. Aloo and a cadre of advisors accompanied the Emperor on this trip. Upon their arrival in one of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star's]] massive [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]], they were greeted by an assemblage of Imperial personnel and [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] as they disembarked from the [[Emperor's personal shuttle/Legends|Emperor's shuttle]]. Aloo and the others joined file behind the Emperor, his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], and a group of [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] as they departed the docking bay<ref name="ROTJ" /> for the [[Emperor's throne room]].<ref name="ROTJ2">[[Return of the Jedi 2|''Return of the Jedi'' 2]]</ref>

Within the throne room, Aloo and fellow advisor Janus Greejatus met with the Emperor and were soon joined by Vader and Moff [[Tiaan Jerjerrod/Legends|Tiaan Jerjerrod]], commander of the Death Star.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Upon Vader's arrival, the dignitaries watched silently as the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] disembarked from the [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]]. Vader made no effort to acknowledge either Aloo or Greejatus, ignoring them as he moved to discuss matters with his [[Sith Master/Legends|master]].<ref name="ROTJjn">[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]</ref> During the meeting, the Emperor instructed Vader to move the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Fleet]] to the far side of Endor, where it would remain until the Rebels launched their attack. Though Vader voiced his concerns of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Fleet]] massing near the planet [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]], the Emperor shrugged them off, confident that his trap would successfully see the end of the Rebellion. Vader and Jerjerrod departed, leaving the Emperor and his two advisors to resume their interrupted gathering. The Alliance soon launched its assault, but the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] ended differently than the Emperor had planned. In the end, Vader, redeemed by his son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], killed Palpatine, and the Alliance destroyed the Death Star.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Aloo and the rest of the Emperor's advisors were obliterated in the battlestation's explosion.<ref name="Galactic Files" />

==Personality and traits==
As the senior political consultant to Palpatine, Sim Aloo almost never spoke and displayed considerable wisdom and patience.<ref name="CCG" /> Collectively, the Imperial Advisors were loyal to the Emperor but, among each other, were politically divided and insecure, always at one another's [[Throat/Legends|throats]].<ref name="GG5" /> Aloo possessed a [[Hold-out blaster/Legends|hold-out blaster]],<ref name="DB" /> which he concealed in the sleeve of his robe.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" /> He stood at a height of 1.85 [[Meter/Legends|meters]], weighed 73 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]<ref name="Chrome Perspectives" /> and had [[Color/Legends|gray]] hair and blue [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />

==Powers and abilities==
Like fellow Inner Circle member Janus Greejatus,<ref name="Greejatus">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Janus Greejatus}}</ref> Aloo was [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-sensitive,<ref name="CCG" /> though his power was low.<ref name="Galactic Files" /> During the time of the Empire, Aloo was one of many advisors to receive training as a Dark Side Adept.<ref name="DSS">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref> As a result, he was capable of manipulating the Force, if only slightly.<ref name="DSS" /> Aloo was exceptionally intelligent and very skilled with diplomacy. The advisor had average speed and fighting ability, and slightly below average strength.<ref name="Galactic Files" />

==Equipment==
Aloo wore lavish [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] that was representative of his homeworld's history.<ref name="GG5" /> While on the Death Star II<ref name="ROTJ" /> in 4 ABY,<ref name="Kren's Galactic Files" /> Aloo wore purple Coruscanti headwear and a crimson vest for show. Over the vest was a high status-indicating lavish robe with expensive underlining. Hidden in the sleeves of his robe was a small blaster.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|On ''Jedi'', one of the most exciting things from a design point of view was the advisers who surround the Emperor. I spent a lot of time trying to figure out what they might look like because I thought it was important that through them you might understand what the Emperor's world is like. Coming from a Catholic background, I sort of made a joke, and that's why they look like bishops. So they wear red, and they have elaborate headgear. This was a challenge because it wasn't in the script, and you see them only briefly in the movie.|Nilo Rodis-Jamero, on the designs of Aloo and the other advisors in ''Return of the Jedi''|<ref name="AS">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>}}
[[File:BTCH01AB.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The characters who would become Aloo and Greejatus appeared in a BlasTech Industries advertisement in ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''.]]
Sim Aloo first appeared, albeit fleetingly, as one of the many unnamed advisors mentioned in the [[1983]] [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="Novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> In the film, Aloo was portrayed by [[Anthony Lang]],<ref name="SWCA">{{SW|url=news/swca-secrets-of-the-mos-eisley-cantina-panel-liveblog|text=SWCA: Secrets of the Mos Eisley Cantina Panel Liveblog|nolive=1}}</ref> appearing briefly in two scenes as one of the unnamed Imperial dignitaries accompanying Emperor Palpatine to the second Death Star.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Lang was uncredited for his appearance. The outfits of the advisors were designed by [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero]], who modeled the clothing off the red garments and the intricate headgear of [[Wikipedia:Catholic Church|Catholic]] [[Wikipedia:Bishop|bishops]].<ref name="AS" />

Prior to Aloo and Greejatus being named, in [[1990]], [[Michael Stern]]'s ''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]'' used an illustration of both of those advisors on the page of a sample Imperial advisor template for another character, [[Kren Blista-Vanee/Legends|Kren Blista-Vanee]].<ref name="GG5" /> In the sourcebook's [[1995]] [[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|second edition]], an individual image of Aloo was also used on the same page as the template for Kren Blista-Vanee.<ref name="GG52">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]]</ref> The character was given a name and a brief backstory in the [[2000]] ''[[Death Star II Limited]]'' expansion set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]].<ref name="CCG" /> Aloo later appeared in the [[2006]] non-[[canon]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] ''[[The Return of Tag & Bink: Special Edition]]'', by [[Kevin Rubio]].<ref name="T&B">''[[The Return of Tag & Bink: Special Edition]]''</ref>

===Non-canon biography===
{{Quote|Something troubles you, my lord?|Sim Aloo|<ref name="T&B" />}}
Sim Aloo plays a minor role in ''The Return of Tag & Bink: Special Edition'', in two scenes aboard the second Death Star. Like in the movie, Aloo is part of the docking bay procession following the Emperor's arrival. The procession differs from that of the film in that Aloo and Greejatus are the only advisors present, and that there are a few additions: namely, protagonists [[Tag Greenly|Tag Greenley]] and [[Bink Otauna/Legends|Bink Otauna]] (disguised as [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guards]]) and two [[Wikipedia:Cylon (1978)|Cylons]] from the [[Wikipedia:Battlestar Galactica (1978 TV series)|''Battlestar Galactica'']] television series. Aloo and Greejatus later appear in the Emperor's throne room, where they discuss Palpatine's disappointment of what [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader had become after his "[[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|accident]]."<ref name="T&B" /> In addition, Aloo also briefly appears in the [[2012]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Kinect Star Wars]], where he is seen in the Emperor's throne room dancing in the background along with Greejatus and many [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="Kinect">''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''</ref>
